title: Snap, Crackle & Pop: Roy Haynesin komppauksen jännitteellisten elementtien analysointi (Arttu Huopainen, Sibelius Academy, Uniarts Helsinki, 2024)
notes: A thesis transcribing his comping on Matrix (Now He Sings, Now He Sobs, 1968) at 288, with bar numbers and limbs: 'overlapping meters atop the piece's 4/4 pulse, such as 3/4 and 6/4'; a 6/4 pattern on the ride for eight bars (24-32); the hat foot in a '2-3 clave-type division' of quarters (61-68, 145-152); threes on the hat with snare dotted quarters (105-109); dotted quarters, 'a three-eighth-note phrase ... a polyrhythmic phenomenon' (5-8, 69-72, 77-84, 117-121, 185-193). Text read in full through a text extraction; the notation images were not seen.

title: Transcription: Roy Haynes – It's Time (Todd Bishop, Cruise Ship Drummer, 16 April 2021)
notes: At 266. 'The tune is in 4, but Haynes is playing with a strong broken up 3 feel all the way through'; 'meter-within-meter', phrases of 'two, three, and four beats'; 'almost straight 8ths, not quite'; the hat sparse, in unison with accents on the bass drum or snare. The post read; the PDF not.

title: Transcription: Roy Haynes – Bad News Blues, parts 01-03 (Todd Bishop, Cruise Ship Drummer, 2017)
notes: 'Lots of unisons, lots of linear things, not a lot of layered independence'; the cymbal in 'a dotted 8th/16th interpretation', sketching a shuffle at times; 'light backbeats'; accents on 'the &s of 4, relatively fewer &s of 3'; snare and bass drum together, the bass accented and the snare ghosted. The posts read; the PDFs not.

title: Transcription: Roy Haynes comping, Bluz for Liz (Todd Bishop, Cruise Ship Drummer, 10 May 2020)
notes: 108 bars of comping: he 'frequently punches the & of 3, or & of 3/& of 4 with a buzzed stroke', 'splashes the hihat with his foot', the bass drum 'sparse'; hands and feet often in unison. The post read; the PDF not.

title: World's shortest Roy Haynes waltz lesson (Todd Bishop, Cruise Ship Drummer)
notes: Windows: exaggerated accents in odd places, triplets between the snare and bass drum, open ruffs. No hemiola named.

title: Transcription: Roy Haynes feature, New Arrival (Todd Bishop, Cruise Ship Drummer, 5 September 2021)
notes: 'Most running eighth notes are straight', the syncopations swung.

title: A 2007 Jazziz article and four interviews with Roy Haynes (Ted Panken, 13 March 2012)
notes: The hat foot: 'I can't even do that if I tried ... I just put my foot on the side, and play it when I want to play it'; 'I dance around the 2 and 4, but it's still there'. Kit: an 18in bass drum, 8x10 and 9x12 toms, a 14 or 16 floor tom, two crashes and an 18in flat ride, a Zildjian copy of 'a flat ride Paiste' on Now He Sings, Now He Sobs. Listened to Blakey and Roach as a teenager; Tito Puente at the Palladium; Elvin 'checked me out'. Read as summaries with quotes.

title: Roy Haynes (Percussive Arts Society Hall of Fame, Rick Mattingly)
notes: Born 13 March 1925, Roxbury, Boston (correcting 1926); Jo Jones his biggest influence; also Shadow Wilson, Kenny Clarke, Max Roach, Art Blakey; 'Snap Crackle', which he credited to George Shearing and Al McKibbon. Read as a summary.

title: Roy Haynes (Modern Drummer, Ira Gitler, May 2004)
notes: Mingus: 'you didn't play the beat, you suggested the beat'; 'I was never a rudimental drummer, so I think my sound comes from my mind more than my hands'. Read as a summary.

title: Roy Haynes on Papa Jo Jones (Scott K. Fish, from Jeff Potter, Modern Drummer, February 1986)
notes: 'Jo Jones had a feeling — a looseness. He had a happy sound.' Read as a summary.

title: Drummer Shortcomings Lead to Innovations Pt 2 – Roy Haynes (Scott K. Fish, 23 September 2020)
notes: He never could hold strict 2 and 4 on the hi-hat, so the foot became a free voice; a white four-piece Ludwig. Read as a summary.

title: Integration and development of jazz drum soloing (Borut Rampih, Research Catalogue)
notes: Eighths and sixteenths 'straight and in front', triplets 'laid back, open and wide'; the hi-hat a separate voice in solos; Bill Stewart and Brian Blade after him. Read as a summary.

title: TT 454: Farewell to Roy Haynes (Ethan Iverson, 2024)
notes: Billy Hart: DeJohnette 'plays like Roy Haynes'; Corea 'made all his drummers use the same flat ride'. Read as a summary.

title: Roy Haynes: Snap Crackle (Alan Kurtz, jazz.com)
notes: The orchestrated drum intro; a solo of sixteenth calls and answers, then offbeat-eighth figures on the toms; 'smaller, high-pitched drums'. Read as a summary.
